info.name: SoundCraft integration
info.summary: Edit audio and SoundCraft sessions in Nextcloud with SoundCraft
info.description:
Open an audio file (WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3, Ogg Vorbis, AAC/M4A, CAF) or a SoundCraft session in Files with **Edit in SoundCraft** and work on it right in the browser, the way you know from a studio workstation: tracks, clips, edits and fades, the mixer with sends and plug-ins, automation, MIDI and bouncing.
- **Save** stores the session as one file, a SoundCraft session bundle (.scraftz) holding the session and its audio, and Nextcloud keeps its previous state as a file version. An audio file opens as a new session of the same name; the first Save asks for the bundle's name and folder (it's offered next to the audio file). - Sessions saved by SoundCraft on a computer (a .scraft file with its Audio Files folder, synced to Nextcloud) open with their audio, and save as a bundle next to them. - **Bounce Mix** and the exports store a file in any folder you pick. - Read-only files open normally; saving offers a copy. - If someone else changes the session while you have it open, you choose whether to replace their version or save a copy. - Optionally, clicking an audio file or a session in Files opens it in SoundCraft.
SoundCraft runs entirely in your browser as WebAssembly. Files go only between your browser and your Nextcloud, and the server needs no extra software.
This is a community integration based on [SoundCraft](https://github.com/storytold/soundcraft) by the ArtCraft team, an open-source, Rust-native audio workstation. It embeds a build of SoundCraft and is not made or endorsed by the ArtCraft team.
**Requirements:** a browser with WebGPU or WebGL2, and a web server that serves `.wasm` files as `application/wasm` (Nextcloud's own Apache and nginx configurations do).
info.author: Britton Couchman
